headline: HSC results: 40,084 students secure GPA-5, pass rate drops to 52.12%
summary: The number of top scorers has plummeted by more than half in two years, while 293 institutions recorded a zero pass rate.
details: A total of 40,084 students achieved the highest grade point average (GPA-5) in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent exams, a sharp decline from 69,097 last year.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced the figures on Saturday, revealing that 20,363 males and 19,721 females secured the top grade.
The overall pass rate for HSC and equivalent examinations has dropped to 52.12%, with pass rates falling across all nine general education boards.
In a stark contrast, 293 educational institutions recorded a zero pass rate, while nearly 600,000 students failed their exams for the second consecutive year.
Dhaka Board topped the pass rate charts, while Barisal recorded the lowest. Madrasa and technical boards also saw declines, with pass rates falling to 61.07% and 49.43% respectively.
A total of 1,270,583 students from 9,439 institutions under 11 education boards sat for the exams across 2,697 centres nationwide.
caption:
GPA-5 achievers plummet by more than half in two years. 40,084 students secure the top grade as the overall pass rate drops to 52.12%.

A total of 40,084 students achieved the highest grade point average (GPA-5) in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent exams, a sharp decline from 69,097 last year.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced the figures on Saturday, revealing that 20,363 males and 19,721 females secured the top grade.

The overall pass rate for HSC and equivalent examinations has dropped to 52.12%, with pass rates falling across all nine general education boards.

In a stark contrast, 293 educational institutions recorded a zero pass rate, while nearly 600,000 students failed their exams for the second consecutive year.

Dhaka Board topped the pass rate charts, while Barisal recorded the lowest. Madrasa and technical boards also saw declines, with pass rates falling to 61.07% and 49.43% respectively.

A total of 1,270,583 students from 9,439 institutions under 11 education boards sat for the exams across 2,697 centres nationwide.

headline_marked: Friend [[arrested in murder case]] over death of former Air Force officer
headline: Friend arrested in murder case over death of former Air Force officer
summary: Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip was detained after Tahsif Souri's father filed a murder case against unknown persons.
details: River Police have arrested Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip, a close associate of former Bangladesh Air Force officer Tahsif Souri, in connection with his death.
Tahsif's father, KM Enayetul Karim, filed a murder case at Uttarkhan Police Station on Friday night, accusing unidentified persons of killing his son.
Dwip had been picked up by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) from his Mohammadpur home on Thursday night for questioning.
River Police recovered Tahsif's floating body from the Rajabari Ghat of the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon.
Investigation reveals Tahsif left home on Tuesday evening after being called by Dwip and the two had dinner together before parting ways near Uttara House Building.
Acting on information provided by Dwip, police recovered Tahsif's motorcycle from the Mazar slum in Tongi on Friday morning.
Dwip admitted to visiting a known drug spot in the Tongi area with Tahsif at midnight on the day of the incident.
The case is now being investigated by the River Police, and Dwip is expected to be sent to court on Saturday.
caption:
A friend is arrested after a former Air Force officer's body was found floating in the Turag River.

River Police have arrested Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip, a close associate of former Bangladesh Air Force officer Tahsif Souri, in connection with his death.

Tahsif's father, KM Enayetul Karim, filed a murder case at Uttarkhan Police Station on Friday night, accusing unidentified persons of killing his son.

Dwip had been picked up by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) from his Mohammadpur home on Thursday night for questioning.

River Police recovered Tahsif's floating body from the Rajabari Ghat of the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon.

Investigation reveals Tahsif left home on Tuesday evening after being called by Dwip and the two had dinner together before parting ways near Uttara House Building.

Acting on information provided by Dwip, police recovered Tahsif's motorcycle from the Mazar slum in Tongi on Friday morning.

Dwip admitted to visiting a known drug spot in the Tongi area with Tahsif at midnight on the day of the incident.

The case is now being investigated by the River Police, and Dwip is expected to be sent to court on Saturday.
